items.title: 7.6 Ethical Issues in Data Science and Analysis

source_refs.note: Topic 7.6 as printed (PDF 101-102, printed 97-98): the Do You Know box, bias with its five numbered examples, ethical use of data and models, responsible communication.

blocks.text: Ethical issues are a major concern in data science and data analysis. As data is collected and analyzed on a large scale, it must be handled responsibly. Ethical practices ensure fairness, accuracy, and trust in data-driven decisions. Poor ethical standards can lead to the misuse of data and harm individuals or groups. Data scientists must follow ethical guidelines while collecting, processing, and interpreting data. Transparency and accountability are essential in every stage of data analysis. Ethical awareness helps maintain public confidence in data science applications.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Biased data can produce unfair results. Ethical data science protects privacy and avoids discrimination. Responsible data use builds trust in technology.
Bias in Data Collection and Analysis

Bias in data collection occurs when data does not fairly represent all groups. This can happen due to limited data sources or unfair sampling methods. Biased data leads to inaccurate and misleading analysis results. During analysis, personal assumptions may also introduce bias. Such bias can affect decision-making and reinforce unfair outcomes. Identifying and mitigating bias is essential for reliable results. Therefore, careful data collection and objective analysis are necessary to ensure fairness. Here are simple examples of bias in data collection and analysis:

items: Survey Bias: A survey about student performance is conducted only in top-performing schools, ignoring average or low-performing schools.
Sampling Bias: A health study includes only young adults, so results do not represent older people.
Gender Bias: A hiring dataset contains mostly male candidates, leading the model to favour male applicants.
Geographical Bias: Data collected only from urban areas is used to make decisions for rural populations.
Confirmation Bias: A researcher focuses only on data that supports their belief and ignores contradictory results.

blocks.text: Ethical Use of Data and Models

Ethical use of data involves respecting privacy and confidentiality of individuals. Data should be collected with proper consent and used only for intended purposes. Machine learning models must be designed to avoid discrimination. Sensitive data should be protected from unauthorized access. Ethical guidelines help prevent misuse of predictive models. Transparency in model design builds trust among users. Responsible use of data and models ensures positive social impact.

Responsible communication of findings is essential in data science. Results should be presented honestly without exaggeration or manipulation. Limitations of the data and analysis must be clearly stated. Misleading visuals or selective reporting should be avoided. Clear explanations help stakeholders understand the results accurately. Ethical communication prevents misinterpretation and misuse of findings. Thus, truthful reporting strengthens credibility and trust in data analysis.
